options: Total wait time by wait type since the instance started (or since the counters were last cleared)
Only waits that happened in the last 60 seconds
A list of currently blocked sessions
The execution plan for every query that has ever run
questions.explain: It's a cumulative, running total per wait_type, reset only on a restart or an explicit DBCC SQLPERF CLEAR.

options: The portion of wait time spent waiting for a CPU to become available after the wait was already satisfied
The total time a query took to run end to end
The time spent waiting for a lock to be granted
The time SQL Server spent compiling an execution plan
questions.explain: Subtracting signal_wait_time_ms from wait_time_ms leaves the genuine resource wait time, separate from CPU queueing.

questions.q: A DBA sees PAGEIOLATCH_SH and PAGEIOLATCH_EX dominating the top of sys.dm_os_wait_stats. What does that generally indicate?
options: The instance is waiting heavily on disk I/O to read data pages into the buffer pool
A deadlock is currently in progress
Statistics are out of date on a major table
The transaction log is full
questions.explain: PAGEIOLATCH waits occur while a task waits for a data page to be physically read from disk — a storage I/O signal.

questions.q: Why filter out wait types like SLEEP_TASK and LAZYWRITER_SLEEP before ranking by wait_time_ms?
options: They're background/idle waits that accumulate constantly and don't indicate a real problem
They are deprecated and no longer tracked by SQL Server
They only appear on Azure SQL Database, never on-premises
They always indicate a critical CPU bottleneck
questions.explain: These are waits generated by background threads idling on purpose — including them just adds noise to the ranking.

questions.q: What does running DBCC SQLPERF(N'sys.dm_os_wait_stats', CLEAR) do?
options: Resets the cumulative wait statistics counters to zero so the next query reflects only activity since the clear
Permanently disables wait statistics collection on the instance
Clears all currently blocked sessions
Removes all rows from sys.dm_os_wait_stats permanently, even after a restart
questions.explain: It's the standard way to take a clean before/after snapshot around a specific workload or troubleshooting window.
